key_insight: Reward models inherit representational value biases from their pretrained LLM initializations, producing systematic differences in reward judgments across value-relevant axes even after RM-specific training.
problem_solved: Addresses the understudied question of how pretraining shapes reward-model behavior and whether value-related biases persist in RMs used for alignment.
method: Empirical evaluation of 10 leading open-weight reward models initialized from pretrained LLMs.
Probing RMs with validated psycholinguistic corpora to elicit value- and preference-related judgments across multiple axes.
Quantitative comparison of model responses to characterize systematic differences and trace them back to pretrained representations.
impact: Shows that alignment via reward modeling can inherit unwanted value biases from pretraining, so practitioners must evaluate and mitigate pretrained influences when building and deploying RMs. Results guide better RM selection, evaluation protocols, and targeted debiasing or fine-tuning strategies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Pretrained LLM → Reward model initialization/fine-tuning → Output judgments (to show inheritance path).
Heatmap or matrix comparing RM responses across multiple value axes (rows = models, columns = value dimensions).
Bar/violin plots of bias magnitude per model illustrating variability across the 10 RMs.
Schematic of probing setup: psycholinguistic corpus → prompt variants → RM scores (to convey methodology concisely).
paper_title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
paper_authors: Brian Christian, Jessica A. F. Thompson, Elle Michelle Yang, Vincent Adam, Hannah Rose Kirk
